headline: Aging-aligned remodeling, cross-species timing, and region-calibrated epigenetic clocks
label: Modeling Biological Aging Trajectories
summary: Generative and clock-based models now separate aging-aligned change from disease remodeling and recalibrate age estimates across species and populations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit population-level or temporal structure imposed on aging data so that inferred age-related variation becomes interpretable. scCody applies a generative optimal-transport framework to single-cell cohorts, learning age-dependent cell population dynamics and separating aging-aligned remodeling from divergent disease-associated remodeling. A cross-species study aligns 11,365 human and canid observations across organ systems and reports that system-level heterochrony models outperform the rule of seven, indicating that diverse clocks govern development and aging pace. A region-specific DNAm SuperLearner epigenetic clock, trained on non-Nicoyan Costa Ricans, calibrates age acceleration for the Nicoya blue zone. What is new across these items is the move away from a single universal age scale toward reference frames defined by cell population, organ system, or regional population, with the explicit structure making age-linked variation controllable and comparable.
